body: This method was no longer called btw.

I'm not sure if its safe to save this as a pointer, if it was a plugin dock it could be deleted.

Also the purpose is to switch away from the game dock, not to focus on the previously opened dock. If that dock is made floating or closed then we don't care about that dock, we only want to switch to another dock in the main screen if there is one.

Currently it can print errors when floating/closing main screen docks in some cases. And it can still focus on the empty Game tab.

Can it use tab container's previous tab instead?
Previous tab works. It further simplified the code.

prev_dock can be null, this should have a check so it doesn't print an error.
In floating with toolbar mode, close all main screen docks, then run the game, then open the game dock from the menu.

It looks like there are some cases where the Game dock can be the previous dock, so this should also check it the previous dock is the game dock. It can fall back to next or previous available tab, or not switch in this case.
To reproduce: in floating with toolbar mode, load the default layout, open the Game dock, then the Asset Store dock, then run the game, then close or float the Asset Store. It switches to the Game dock when it shouldn't.

I'm getting an issue where a main dock is unable to be opened.
In floating with toolbar mode, load default layout, open 2D dock, run game, click on Game dock, close 2D dock. 2D cannot be opened again from the menu. A layout has to be loaded to fix it. It becomes marked as open but is child to the closed dock parent.
When closing the dock, `_move_dock` tries to switch to the previous tab before removing it. This is the game dock which changes focus back to the dock that is in the middle of closing, which marks it as open.
Not sure the best way to fix it.
I intentionally left the errors, as it's not really valid to have a null here, but I can remove it.
Not sure why its not valid when the user can trigger it?

Because it makes the Game tab appear while in invalid state, which this PR tries to avoid. But I suppose it can't be prevented if all other tabs are closed. Maybe I'll just add a Label that appears when the tab is empty.
This label increases the minimum size when its shown. I don't think it causes problems but it should probably wrap or trim.

I wonder if it would be better to use iterate_children for these, the current child can be gotten beforehand for the check.
Probably relevant for other places as well. Not needed for this PR.

This isn't really accurate for the user, Android has a similar game toolbar when running projects, and the Game dock button is important as the only way to re-open a running project. As is the user might think it should be closed as useless.
I think this should have a similar message on desktop, like "The game runs in a picture-in-picture window with an attached toolbar." or something.
`iterate_children()` does not apply here, because this loop does not go over all children and the loop index is needed.

Well, the picture-in-picture window is not the Game dock.
You can run into this label only if you close all other main screens, so most people will never see it.
I realized this only operates on the current control, so it doesn't need a loop and can use `get_current_tab_control()`.

It's not technically the same thing, but the picture-in-picture window with the toolbar has the same functionality. And the game dock is used even as just a button. So I think it doesn't help the user to say its not available.
Though I agree it would be rare to see.
It's rare to see but it's still a regression compared to the previous behavior.
